invented.quote: **Subject: Three office days a week from 1 September 2027**
invented.why: The brief states the change starts on September 1, but does not state the year is 2027.

invented.quote: From 1 September 2027, everyone at the firm will work in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
invented.why: The brief gives the date as September 1, without specifying the year 2027.

invented.quote: You can keep working remotely until 31 December 2027.
invented.why: The brief says they can keep working remotely 'until the end of next year' (which would be at least 16 months after September 1 of the current year), whereas the writer invented the year 2027 and collapsed 'the end of next year' into the end of the same year the policy starts.

invented.quote: From January 2028, we're asking you to come in one day a week.
invented.why: The brief states this requirement begins after 'the end of next year' without giving the year 2028.

invented.quote: I know that gives you only four months longer than everyone else.
invented.why: The brief states the four remote staff have 'until the end of next year' (which would be 16 months after a September 1 start in the current year), not four months within the same calendar year.
